meta.executive_summary: The current DIGIT/CMS deployment presents an unacceptable security posture for handling confidential citizen grievance data, primarily driven by systemic perimeter and configuration failures. With 41 services—including critical datastores and admin UIs—bound directly to 0.0.0.0 without an active host firewall (ufw), the platform relies entirely on cloud security groups as a single point of failure. Compounded by default credentials, Docker socket mounts, and unauthenticated public endpoints, the environment is one misconfiguration away from full data exposure. Immediate remediation must focus on hardening network bindings, enforcing strict host firewalls, and purging default credentials.
priority_actions: Activate and configure the host firewall (ufw) immediately to restrict traffic, ensuring datastores (PostgreSQL, Redis, Kafka, MinIO) and admin UIs (Grafana, Prometheus, Jupyter) are strictly bound to localhost or internal interfaces rather than 0.0.0.0.
Rotate all weak, default credentials found in the deployment configuration and ensure secrets are injected securely rather than stored in plain text within the public repository.
Remove Docker socket mounts and sensitive host directory volumes from containers to eliminate immediate container-to-host privilege escalation vectors.
Audit and secure the nginx configuration to close unauthenticated admin/API surfaces and enforce missing security headers such as HSTS and nosniff.
Harden the CI/CD and deployment pipeline by replacing direct remote script piping into shells and insecure HTTP registry usage with verified, checksum-validated artifacts.

findings.title: Datastore or admin port published on all interfaces (0.0.0.0)
findings.why: Publishing ports like postgres-db (15432:5432) and prometheus (19090:9090) on all interfaces (0.0.0.0) exposes internal databases and monitoring dashboards directly to the public internet, allowing unauthenticated attackers to read/write sensitive complaint and telemetry data.
findings.fix:
Bind the ports strictly to localhost in `docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml` under the respective services:
```yaml
ports:
  - "127.0.0.1:19090:9090"
# and for postgres:
ports:
  - "127.0.0.1:15432:5432"
```

triage.reason: Postgres and Prometheus ports are published to 0.0.0.0 with no host firewall active.

findings.title: Weak or default credential in deployment config
findings.why: Hardcoding default fallback credentials like `eGov@123` or `admin` in deployment scripts allows attackers with repository access or compromised environments to easily authenticate against Keycloak and OpenBao.
findings.fix:
Remove insecure default fallback strings from sensitive credential templates in the Ansible deployment tasks:
```yaml
TOKEN_EXCHANGE_SYSTEM_PASSWORD={{ kcprep_secrets.json.data.data.token_exchange_system_password }}
```

triage.reason: Hardcoded default fallback password eGov@123 used in token exchange configuration.

findings.title: Volume Has Sensitive Host Directory
findings.why: Mounting sensitive host directories like `/var/lib/docker/containers` and `/proc` into monitoring or logging containers gives read access to host-level container stdout/stderr logs and process trees, potentially leaking secrets passed via environment variables.
findings.fix: This is expected behavior for log collection and metrics agents (Promtail and Node Exporter). Ensure the mounts are read-only (`:ro`) and restrict host access to trusted administrators.

triage.reason: Mounts of host proc/sys for node_exporter and docker logs for promtail are read-only and necessary.

findings.title: Docker Socket Mounted In Container
findings.why: Mounting the Docker socket (`/var/run/docker.sock`) into containers grants root-level code execution on the host machine, as any process inside the container can interact with the Docker daemon to spin up privileged containers or mount host roots.
findings.fix: Verify that containers requiring the Docker socket (like telemetry or log agents) are strictly necessary and restricted from untrusted networks. Alternatively, replace direct socket access with a secured API proxy.

triage.reason: Mounting docker.sock permits container escape and full root host takeover even if read-only.

findings.title: Remote script piped directly into a shell
findings.why: Piping remote scripts directly into bash (`curl ... | bash -`) enables man-in-the-middle attackers to inject malicious execution code into the provisioning pipeline, leading to remote code execution on the host.
findings.fix:
Download the script to a temporary file, inspect or verify its checksum, and then execute it via Ansible:
```yaml
- name: Download NodeSource setup script
  ansible.builtin.get_url:
    url: https://deb.nodesource.com/setup_20.x
    dest: /tmp/nodesource_setup.sh
    mode: '0700'
- name: Execute Node installation script
  ansible.builtin.command: /tmp/nodesource_setup.sh
```

triage.reason: Piping remote script directly to bash from curl risks MITM and arbitrary remote code execution.

findings.title: Docker image registry used over insecure HTTP
findings.why: Enabling insecure registries permits plain-http communication with container registries, exposing the deployment stack to Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacks where container images can be intercepted and replaced with malicious binaries.
findings.fix:
Remove insecure registries from the Docker daemon configuration in the Ansible task:
```yaml
'insecure-registries': []
```

triage.reason: Insecure Docker HTTP registries allow man-in-the-middle attacks on container images during pull.

findings.title: SSH host-key verification disabled
findings.why: Disabling SSH host key checking (`StrictHostKeyChecking=no`) leaves the deployment automation vulnerable to Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacks when connecting to remote servers during setup.
findings.fix: Remove `ansible_ssh_common_args: '-o StrictHostKeyChecking=no'` from the generated inventory block and rely on known_hosts management.

triage.reason: StrictHostKeyChecking=no disables SSH host verification, enabling man-in-the-middle attacks.

findings.title: Unauthenticated admin/API surface exposed via nginx
findings.why: Exposing administrative endpoints like `/mcp` without authentication via Nginx allows any external user to invoke administrative tool actions such as user creation or tenant bootstrapping.

triage.reason: Nginx exposes unauthenticated administrative /mcp endpoints directly to clients.

findings.title: Container Capabilities Unrestricted
findings.why: Running containers with unrestricted capabilities allows container breakout if an application vulnerability is exploited, granting the attacker extended privileges inside the host kernel.
findings.fix:
Drop all capabilities by default and only add back required ones in `docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml`:
```yaml
security_opt:
  - no-new-privileges:true
cap_drop:
  - ALL
```

triage.reason: Containers do not drop default Linux capabilities (cap_drop: ALL missing).

findings.title: Security Opt Not Set
findings.why: Omitting security options like `no-new-privileges` can allow processes inside the container to gain new privileges through `setuid` or `setgid` binaries during an exploit.
findings.fix:
Add security options to the service definition in `docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml`:
```yaml
security_opt:
  - no-new-privileges:true
```

triage.reason: Missing no-new-privileges:true security option allows privilege escalation via setuid binaries.

findings.title: Container Traffic Not Bound To Host Interface
findings.why: Binding container ports without specifying a loopback IP exposes backend services directly to external network interfaces instead of restricting them to local proxy routing.
findings.fix:
Explicitly bind container ports to localhost in `docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml`:
```yaml
ports:
  - "127.0.0.1:18095:8090"
```

triage.reason: Service ports bind to 0.0.0.0 on host without firewall, bypassing intended reverse proxy.

findings.title: Healthcheck Not Set
findings.why: Failing to define a healthcheck for critical backend services prevents container orchestrators and monitoring tools from detecting deadlocks or crashed application states automatically.
findings.fix:
Add a healthcheck block to the service definition in `docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml`:
```yaml
healthcheck:
  test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:8080/actuator/health >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1"]
  interval: 30s
  timeout: 10s
  retries: 3
```

triage.reason: Missing container healthcheck is a reliability issue rather than an exploitable security vulnerability.

findings.title: Ensure that HTTPS url is used with uri
findings.why: Using unencrypted HTTP endpoints for internal service preparation (such as OpenBao sealing/unsealing) transmits tokens and secrets in cleartext over the network.
findings.fix: Ensure internal URIs enforce HTTPS where applicable, or restrict communication strictly to secure local loops (`127.0.0.1`).

triage.reason: URI request communicates over loopback 127.0.0.1 directly to local OpenBao container.

findings.title: File created without an explicit restrictive mode
findings.why: Creating configuration or state files without explicit restrictive modes (e.g., `mode: '0600'`) may expose sensitive environment variables or secrets to unprivileged users on the host.
findings.fix:
Explicitly set safe file permissions in Ansible tasks:
```yaml
file:
  path: "{{ digit_dir }}/.env"
  mode: '0600'
```

triage.reason: Directory creation without explicit restrictive mode leaves permissions to default umask.

findings.title: Ensure that certificate validation isn't disabled with uri
findings.why: Disabling certificate validation (`validate_certs: false`) during URI validation calls leaves API health checks vulnerable to MitM interception.
findings.fix:
Enable certificate validation in Ansible URI tasks:
```yaml
validate_certs: true
```

triage.reason: Disabling TLS certificate validation when tls_enabled is false permits MITM during validation.

findings.title: Privileged Ports Mapped In Container
findings.why: Mapping privileged ports (< 1024) directly from containers can expose administrative or sensitive entrypoints if not properly guarded.
findings.fix:
Map container ports to unprivileged high-numbered ports on the host interface in `docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml`:
```yaml
ports:
  - "127.0.0.1:18080:80"
```

triage.reason: Mapping container port 80 to high host port 18080 is standard and non-privileged on host.

findings.title: Shell pipeline without pipefail (failures go undetected)
findings.why: Executing shell pipelines without `set -o pipefail` hides intermediate command failures (e.g., preceding grep or docker commands failing), leading to silent deployment errors.
findings.fix:
Prepend `set -euo pipefail;` to shell execution blocks in Ansible:
```yaml
ansible.builtin.shell: |
  set -euo pipefail
  docker ps -a ...
```

triage.reason: Ansible shell commands using pipelines without pipefail allow silent failure of subcommands.

findings.title: Host Namespace is Shared
findings.why: Sharing host namespaces (`pid: host`) exposes the host's process tree and namespaces to the container, breaking container isolation.
findings.fix: Ensure host namespaces are only enabled for specialized monitoring agents (like node-exporter) and restricted from application containers.

triage.reason: Host PID namespace is legitimately required for node_exporter host metric gathering.

findings.title: Memory Not Limited
findings.why: Failing to limit container memory allows a runaway process or memory leak to consume all available host RAM, causing a Denial of Service (DoS) for the entire server.
findings.fix:
Add resource limit blocks to services in `docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml`:
```yaml
deploy:
  resources:
    limits:
      memory: 512M
```

triage.reason: Omission of container memory resource limits is an availability/reliability concern.

findings.title: systemd service runs without hardening (NoNewPrivileges=true)
findings.why: Systemd services running without hardening directives like `NoNewPrivileges=true` can be exploited to escalate privileges via setuid binaries if compromised.
findings.fix:
Add hardening directives to the systemd service template file:
```ini
[Service]
NoNewPrivileges=true
ProtectSystem=full
```

triage.reason: Integration runner systemd service lacks NoNewPrivileges and hardening directives.

findings.title: systemd service runs without hardening (a non-root User=)
findings.why: Systemd services running without hardening directives like `NoNewPrivileges=true` can be exploited to escalate privileges via setuid binaries if compromised.
findings.fix:
Add hardening directives to the systemd service template file:
```ini
[Service]
NoNewPrivileges=true
ProtectSystem=full
```

triage.reason: Integration runner systemd service lacks NoNewPrivileges and hardening directives.

findings.title: systemd service runs without hardening (ProtectSystem=)
findings.why: Systemd services running without hardening directives like `NoNewPrivileges=true` can be exploited to escalate privileges via setuid binaries if compromised.
findings.fix:
Add hardening directives to the systemd service template file:
```ini
[Service]
NoNewPrivileges=true
ProtectSystem=full
```

triage.reason: Integration runner systemd service lacks NoNewPrivileges and hardening directives.

findings.title: nginx is missing the security header: server_tokens off
findings.why: Omitting `server_tokens off;` in Nginx configurations exposes the exact web server version to attackers, aiding in targeting known software vulnerabilities.
findings.fix: Add `server_tokens off;` inside the HTTP or server block of the Nginx configuration template.

triage.reason: Missing server_tokens off in public nginx reveals exact web server versions to clients.

findings.title: nginx is missing the security header: Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS)
findings.why: Omitting `server_tokens off;` in Nginx configurations exposes the exact web server version to attackers, aiding in targeting known software vulnerabilities.
findings.fix: Add `server_tokens off;` inside the HTTP or server block of the Nginx configuration template.

triage.reason: Missing server_tokens off in public nginx reveals exact web server versions to clients.

findings.title: nginx is missing the security header: X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
findings.why: Omitting `server_tokens off;` in Nginx configurations exposes the exact web server version to attackers, aiding in targeting known software vulnerabilities.
findings.fix: Add `server_tokens off;` inside the HTTP or server block of the Nginx configuration template.

triage.reason: Missing server_tokens off in public nginx reveals exact web server versions to clients.

findings.title: Security lint rule disabled in .ansible-lint
findings.why: Disabling security linter rules in `.ansible-lint` can allow insecure configurations and bad practices to propagate into production playbooks unchecked.
findings.fix: Re-enable relevant security rules in `.ansible-lint` and address any underlying warnings directly in the playbooks.

triage.reason: Disabling risky-file-permissions in ansible-lint suppresses warnings on insecure file permissions.

findings.title: Shared Volumes Between Containers
findings.why: Sharing volumes between containers can create implicit coupling and potential privilege or data leakage paths if permissions are overly permissive.
findings.fix: Ensure shared volumes use read-only flags (`:ro`) wherever possible in `docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml`.

triage.reason: Shared read-only mount of Java agent and local tempo data volume is standard and constrained.

findings.title: Cpus Not Limited
findings.why: Unbounded CPU usage by containers can lead to CPU starvation for critical system processes and other microservices during high load or denial-of-service events.
findings.fix:
Add CPU limits under service deploy configurations in `docker-compose.egov-digit.yaml`:
```yaml
deploy:
  resources:
    limits:
      cpus: '1.0'
```

triage.reason: Missing CPU limits is a resource management/reliability control.
